title: Accelerated corneal cross-linking with hypo-osmolar riboflavin in thin keratoconic corneas: 2-year follow-up

license.statement: CC BY 4.0 (article <license>: Creative Commons Attribution License)

groups.description: Epithelium-off accelerated CXL (UVA 9 mW/cm2 for 10 min) with hypo-osmolar 0.1% riboflavin (MedioCROSS H) applied until the thinnest point reached 400 um, in progressive keratoconus with stromal thickness 330-400 um; 28 eyes of 24 patients; retrospective single-arm series; no cataract or other surgery in the described session

series.notes: mean ± SD; BCVA with eyeglasses, recorded in logMAR (Methods; Table 1 footnote 'BCVA= best-corrected visual acuity (logMAR)'); table header N=28; per-visit n not reported

notes: Table 1 also tabulates astigmatism, flattest and steepest keratometry, thinnest-point corneal thickness, uncorrected acuity (logMAR) and contrast sensitivity; Table 2 tabulates higher-order aberrations; none of these is used.
The abstract lists assessments at 1, 3, 6, 12 and 24 months; the Methods and Table 1 give 1, 6, 12 and 24 months (no 3-month column), so no 3-month value exists.
28 eyes of 24 patients: some patients contribute both eyes.
Asterisks in Table 1 mark statistical significance versus pre-CXL; they are not part of the value.
